Master local advertising on Google with expert strategies for Local Services Ads, Maps, and Performance Max to attract nearby customers and grow your business.

## Which Local Advertising Option on Google Fits Your Business?

**Local advertising on Google has three main paths:** Local Services Ads help eligible service businesses get calls and messages, with charges based on leads. Search ads with location information can bring nearby customers to your website, phone, or store. Performance Max campaigns with store goals can promote a physical location across Google, including Maps. Choose based on what you need most: **service leads, website inquiries, or store visits**.

The right choice also depends on what happens after someone finds you. An ad may earn a call, but your reviews, business information, and response time help turn that interest into a customer. This guide will help you compare the options, track results, and decide where to focus.

I’m Tomasz Lasota, founder of WWS - Web Development + SEO in Des Plaines. For owners searching “local advertising google,” I draw on more than 22 years of experience helping businesses grow through Google Ads, local SEO, and websites built to convert.

](https://www.savoirmanagement.com/blog)

# Google Ads for Local Businesses: How to Win Customers in Your Area

How shops, clinics and service businesses use Google Ads to reach nearby customers: location targeting, local keywords, assets, budgets and common pitfalls.

Category

Google Ads

Published

September 19, 2026

Author

Paulestini Francois

Read Time

7 min read

![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/MQtiwlHu4dIqvu3R4tIvZCke0.png?width=1024&height=688)

Quick answer

Google Ads works for local businesses when campaigns target a tight radius around your service area, bid on "service + city" and "near me" keywords, show call and location assets linked to your Google Business Profile, and run during the hours you can serve customers. Start with a small daily budget, track calls and directions as conversions, and add Local Services Ads if your category is eligible.

Key facts

*   **Location targeting:** Target a radius, city or ZIP codes, and set the option to reach people in or regularly in your area.
    
*   **Local keywords:** "Service + city," "near me" and neighborhood names signal ready-to-buy local intent.
    
*   **Assets:** Location assets show your address and distance; call assets add a tap-to-call button.
    
*   **Business Profile:** Relevance, distance and prominence drive local rankings on Google.
    
*   **Budget:** Many local businesses start at $15 to $50 per day.
    

**Google Ads for local businesses** works differently from national campaigns. You are not trying to reach everyone, only people close enough to visit, call or book. That changes how you target, what you bid on and how you measure success. Here is the local playbook we use for shops, clinics and service businesses at Savoir Management.

## Why should local businesses use Google Ads?

**Local searches often come from people ready to act, such as "emergency plumber near me" or "dentist open Saturday." Google Ads puts your business at the top of those results immediately, while organic local rankings take months to build.**

Ads also give you control over where and when you show, so you only pay for clicks from your service area during hours you can respond.

## How do you target your neighborhood with precision?

**Target a radius or list of cities and ZIP codes that matches your real service area, choose "presence" targeting so ads reach people in or regularly in those places, and adjust bids for the closest areas.**

Google explains the options in [About targeting geographic locations](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2453995). For local campaigns:

*   Use a radius of 5 to 15 miles for shops and clinics, wider for mobile services.
    
*   Exclude areas you do not serve.
    
*   Raise bids for the nearest neighborhoods if they convert better.
    

![Infographic of local targeting: a map with a radius around a shop, geo-targeting, local keywords and ad scheduling for local peaks](https://framerusercontent.com/images/QAS5nXetIEnfMDTzVR3j7KJfimY.png)

## Which keywords work best for local businesses?

**The best local keywords combine your service with a place or proximity: "roof repair Austin," "pediatric dentist near me," "dog groomer in Brooklyn." These searches show both need and location.**

*   Use [phrase and exact match](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/7478529) for service + city terms.
    
*   Include neighborhood names and nearby landmarks.
    
*   Add negatives for jobs, training, DIY and locations you do not serve.
    

## Which ad assets matter most for local ads?

**Location and call assets matter most. Location assets show your address, distance and directions from your Google Business Profile, and call assets let mobile searchers call with one tap.**

Set up [location assets](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2404182) and [call assets](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2453991), and add sitelinks for your main services and booking page. See Google's overview of [assets](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/7331111).

## How does your Google Business Profile affect local ads?

**Your Business Profile powers location assets and supports your visibility in Maps and the local pack. Google ranks local results mainly on relevance, distance and prominence, so a complete, accurate profile helps both paid and organic results.**

Read Google's [tips to improve your local ranking](https://support.google.com/business/answer/7091) and follow the [guidelines for representing your business](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177). Keep hours, categories, photos and reviews current.

## How should a local business budget for Google Ads?

**Start with $15 to $50 per day focused on your top two or three services, measure cost per call or booking, and raise the budget only on campaigns that hit your target. A small, focused budget beats a large, scattered one.**

![Barbershop owner planning a monthly ad budget in his chair after hours](https://framerusercontent.com/images/tYfJSkC9qrYhsyXRzRRNVJP52lY.png)

A simple local budget formula:

1.  Average job value: $400
    
2.  Target cost per customer: $80
    
3.  Close rate on calls: 40%, so a target cost per call of $32
    
4.  Daily budget for about three calls a day: roughly $100, or start at $50 and grow
    

## When should you schedule local ads?

**Run ads when you can answer the phone or accept bookings, and raise bids during your busiest hours. Calls that go to voicemail waste money.**

Use [ad scheduling](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2404244) to match staffed hours, or run 24/7 only if you offer emergency service or online booking.

## Should local businesses use Local Services Ads?

**If your category is eligible, yes.** [**Local Services Ads**](https://business.google.com/us/ad-solutions/local-service-ads/) **charge per lead instead of per click and appear above regular search ads with a verification badge, which builds trust with local searchers.**

Run them alongside Search campaigns and compare cost per booked job.

## How should local businesses track calls and visits?

**Track phone calls from ads and from your website as conversions, track form submissions and bookings, and use location assets to measure actions such as direction requests. Calls are often the most valuable local conversion.**

Google Ads can [track conversions](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/1722054) from calls made directly from ads and from calls to a number on your website. Set a minimum call length so short misdials do not count. Ask new customers how they found you, and compare busy periods with ad activity. Together these signals show whether local ads drive real business, not just clicks.

## How do reviews affect local ad performance?

**Reviews influence whether searchers trust you enough to click and call. Strong ratings in your Google Business Profile support ads that
